issues.description: Captures any issues that occurred while deserializing from filesystem

useArtifactHub.description:
If true, the C3 library manager will use the {@link ArtifactHub} to fetch libraries when installing environments instead of fetching
them directly from the repository declared in its config. If false, the C3 Npm library manager will use the npm registry in the
{@link NpmLibraryManager.Config} to fetch packages and the C3 Conda library manager will use the artifacthub to fetch libraries directly
from the Conda and PyPI repositories declared in the {@link CondaLibraryManager.Config}.

channelAlias.description:
This corresponds to the {@link https://conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/user-guide/configuration/use-condarc.html#set-ch-alias channel_alias} parameter in the conda configuration file.
For every {@link ImplLanguage.Library#repository repository} mentioned in a python {@link ImplLanguage.Runtime runtime} that is not
a url, the C3 Conda library manager will prepend this url and the full url will be used as the channel url. So if the
{@link CondaLibraryManager.Config#channelAlias channelAlias} is set as https://conda.anaconda.org, the full url for the conda channel
"conda-forge" will be https://conda.anaconda.org/conda-forge.

defaultChannels.description:
This corresponds to the {@link https://conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/user-guide/configuration/use-condarc.html#default-channels default_channels} parameter in the conda configuration file.
If you have "defaults" as {@link ImplLanguage.Library#repository repository} mentioned in an {@link ImplLanguage.Runtime runtime} then the
C3 Conda library manager will use every Conda channel specified in the default channels to search for a package.

customChannels.description:
This is a map from channel name to channel location
Channels present in customChannels override the channelAlias value. For example, to override the channel location of the 'pkgs/main' channel where the url to repodata is
https://my-local-repo.org/packages/pkgs/main/linux-64/repodata.json
add an entry 'pkgs/main: https://my-local-repo.org/packages/pkgs/main'.

trustedHostsPPI.description:
List of hosts or host:port pairs which will be marked as trusted by Python Package Index, even though it does not have valid or any HTTPS.
More information about {@link https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/cli/pip/#cmdoption-trusted-host trusted host} in Python Package Index.

pipSocketTimeout.description:
This represents the socket timeout in seconds for pip commands. See parameter --timeout at
{@link https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/cli/pip/ pip usage}.

packageCachePath.description: Override the default location of the {@link https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/23.1.x/user-guide/configuration/use-condarc.html#specify-pkg-directories conda packages directory}.

defaultInstallRuntimeTimeout.description: Timeout duration for install runtime process. The default seeded value is an hour.

defaultResolveRuntimeTimeout.description: Timeout duration for resolve runtime process. The default seeded value is an hour.

installRuntimeTimeouts.description:
Overrides default install runtime timeout.
Key is a resolved runtime name. Accuracy of the name is important to make sure appropriate overridden time gets allocated during installation.
Value is timeout duration. Install runtime will fail if not completed within the specified duration. Retry installing or increasing the timeout duration if it repeats.

resolveRuntimeTimeouts.description:
Overrides default resolve runtime timeout.
Key is a resolved runtime name. Accuracy of the name is important to make sure appropriate overridden time gets allocated during resolution.
Value is timeout duration. Resolve runtime will fail if not completed within the specified duration. Retry resolving or increasing the timeout duration if it repeats.

otherOptions.description:
Allows to setup any conda options (that can be set as conda env vars during install/resolve runtime).
These env variables are ephemeral and persist only during the conda runtime installation/resolution. Adding/Removal/Validity is controlled by the admins solely.
Only boolean, numbers and string based config values are supported. Complex configuration like list/dictionaries are not fully supported, please verify.
{@link ImplLanguage.RuntimeBase#installEnvVars} specified as part of a resolved runtime JSON config for a runtime, gets precedence over these global options.
Already predefined options (like extraSafetyChecks, customChannels, etc.) in the config will be ignored from being overridden.
Please follow {@link https://docs.conda.io/projects/conda/en/latest/configuration.html to know about all the configurations and their usage.}

Example code snippet:

```js
var c3Map = C3.Map.ofStrToStr("VERBOSITY", "4", "SSL_VERIFY", "false"); //To see detailed logs (use verbosity at level > 0 when debugging only) and no ssl verification.
CondaLibraryManager.config().setConfigValue("otherOptions", c3Map)
```

title: Type for specifying different configurations used by {@link CondaLibraryManager}.
